standard_prerequisites.name: Domination tested by universal injectivity of a pushout
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the counted proof at lines 22582-22584
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the domination requirement into universal injectivity of a map out of the pushout.

core_obligations: Write M as a directed colimit of finitely presented modules and use the characterisation to reduce to producing, for each i, an index j at least i whose comparison map to M dominates the other (proof lines 22568-22572).
Form the pushout square of the two comparison maps and note that the requirement is equivalent to universal injectivity of the map from M_j to the pushout (proof lines 22575-22584).
Tensor the square with S, use the Mittag-Leffler property of the base change to find j, and conclude by faithful flatness that universal injectivity descends (proof lines 22585-22598).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a domination statement via the characterisation (proof lines 22567-22572).
Convert domination into universal injectivity of a pushout and descend it by faithful flatness (proof lines 22574-22599).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if R to S is faithfully flat and the base change of M is Mittag-Leffler over S, then M is Mittag-Leffler over R (statement lines 22558-22565). The proof does not argue with the definition directly: it reduces the claim through the characterisation to producing an index over which one comparison map dominates another, rewrites that domination as universal injectivity of the map from the approximating module to a pushout, transports the picture along the flat base change, and then uses faithful flatness to bring the universal injectivity back down (proof lines 22567-22599). Choosing the pushout formulation so that faithful flatness applies is the step that carries the argument. H2.
